---
title: "Airport surface events"
description: "How OPDI finds when an aircraft enters and leaves a taxiway, an apron, a stand, a runway threshold area, a hangar or a de-icing pad."
---

## In one sentence

An `entry-{element}` event marks when an aircraft enters an area of an
airport, and the matching `exit-{element}` event when it leaves it, where
`{element}` is the kind of area.

## What it needs

- The airport layout from OpenStreetMap, the open map of the world, for the
  large and medium airports: the areas mapped there as taxiways, aprons,
  stands, threshold markings, hangars and de-icing pads.
- Reports of the track with a position on the airport surface, at an airport
  that the flight list names for the flight (the departure or destination
  airport, or one of the other close airports listed).

## How it is computed

### The layout

1. Each area is read from OpenStreetMap. An area mapped as a line (a taxiway
   centre line) or a point (a stand) is widened into a surface, with the
   width given in OpenStreetMap or a default width for its kind (for example
   30 m for a taxiway and 25 m for a stand).
2. Each surface is covered with H3 cells of resolution 12, each about 300 m²
   (about 20 m across). H3 is an open grid that divides the Earth into
   hexagons.

### Passages

3. **Reports used.** A report flagged on the ground by the transponder is
   always used. A report not flagged on the ground is used only when it is at
   most 300 ft above the airport and at most 50 kt fast (the speed is the
   largest of the reported speed and the speeds from its positions to the
   reports just before and after it, when at most 30 s apart; a report with no
   known speed is used). Aircraft on approach, climbing out or passing low
   over the airport are left out.
4. **Match.** A report is in an area when its H3 cell is one of the area's
   cells.
5. **Passage.** The matched reports of one track in one area, in time order,
   form a passage. A silence of more than 300 s starts a new passage. A
   passage of a single report, or whose first and last reports fall in the
   same second, is dropped.
6. **One area per passage.** Areas of one kind often overlap (a taxiway drawn
   as several lines, a stand drawn over a taxi lane). The area is chosen once
   per passage, so every entry has its exit on the same area: of passages of
   one kind that start (or end) at the same report, the longest is kept, but
   of stands the shortest (the stand itself rather than a larger area drawn
   around it). Where a stand is drawn inside a larger stand area, both
   passages are published, and the larger one is marked
   `info.encloses_stand`.
7. **Parked aircraft.** Two consecutive passages of one area are joined when
   the aircraft moved less than 165 ft (about 50 m) between them and entered
   no other area in between. A parked aircraft whose position jitters across
   the edge of an area then gives one passage. Stand passages are not joined:
   the exit before a silence at the stand is often the off-block.
8. **Events.** The first report of a passage gives the `entry-` event and the
   last gives the `exit-` event, each with that report's position, altitude
   and measurements.
9. **Marks.** `info.at_track_start` is set on an entry made at the track's
   first report with a position, and `info.at_track_end` on an exit made at
   its last: reception started or stopped there, the aircraft did not move.
   `info.ground_only` is set on the events of a track that never leaves the
   ground and whose aircraft type is unknown or a vehicle type, in practice
   an airport vehicle.
10. The [plausibility checks](plausibility-checks.qmd) remove an entry or exit
    made while the aircraft flies (more than 1,500 ft above the airport,
    faster than 80 kt and no report on the ground within 60 s).

The runway itself has no surface event: its use is described by the
[runway events](take-off-landing.qmd).

### By kind of area

| `{element}` | Area | What a passage usually means |
|---|---|---|
| `taxiway` | A path between runways and parking areas | Taxiing; one aircraft passes several taxiways in a row. |
| `apron` | An area where aircraft park, board and load | Arriving at or leaving the parking area. |
| `parking_position` | One stand | Parked at a stand; the passages are used for the [block times](block-times.qmd). |
| `threshold` | The threshold markings at a runway end | An aircraft on the ground near the threshold, usually lining up. Not the landing crossing of the threshold, which is `xing-runway-threshold`. |
| `hangar` | A building for keeping or maintaining aircraft | Into or out of a hangar, often with few reports inside. |
| `deicing_pad` | An area where ice is removed before take-off | The pad area was passed; it does not show that the aircraft was de-iced. |

## Based on

- The method of mapping an airport's layout onto the H3 grid comes from
  [HexAeroPy](../resources.qmd#ref-hexaeropy) (Goens, EUROCONTROL), the tool that finds the
  airports, runways, taxiways and stands used by a flight from its positions.
- The airport areas come from [OpenStreetMap](../resources.qmd#ref-osm-aeroway) (its
  `aeroway` features); the grid is [H3](../resources.qmd#ref-h3).
- The passage rules (steps 3 to 9) were developed for OPDI.
- Related published work: [Olive, Waltert and Schultz (2025)](../resources.qmd#ref-olive-2025)
  also match ADS-B positions on the ground to OpenStreetMap taxiways, to
  measure taxi times and congestion.

## What is published

Event types `entry-taxiway`, `exit-taxiway`, `entry-apron`, `exit-apron`,
`entry-parking_position`, `exit-parking_position`, `entry-threshold`,
`exit-threshold`, `entry-hangar`, `exit-hangar`, `entry-deicing_pad` and
`exit-deicing_pad`, with position, altitude, `distance_flown_nm` and
`time_passed_s`. Their `info` holds `osm_id` (identifier of the area in
OpenStreetMap), `osm_aeroway` (its kind), `osm_ref` (its name or number, when
it has one), `osm_airport`, `opdi_time_in_use_s` (time spent in the area, in
seconds), `osn_icao24`, `osn_flight_id` and, where they apply,
`at_track_start`, `at_track_end`, `ground_only` and `encloses_stand` (see the
[Data dictionary](../data/dictionary.qmd#info-fields)).

## Use cases

- **Taxi routes**: the sequence of `entry-taxiway` events of one flight, from
  stand to runway, for example to compare routes per runway direction.
- **Apron and stand occupancy**: aircraft present per apron or stand and
  hour, from the pairs of entry and exit and `opdi_time_in_use_s`.
- **Time spent at a de-icing pad** in winter, from the pairs of
  `entry-deicing_pad` and `exit-deicing_pad`.

## Limitations

The events exist only where the airport has ground reception and a mapped
layout; vehicles also carry transponders. See
[Limitations: airport surface](../limitations.qmd#lim-surface).

## Availability and accuracy

No record gives the passages themselves. The stand passages are compared with
the recorded block times, which they should be close to.
